capabilities: Assign primary, long-press, and swipe commands to toolbar buttons
Customize button colors, icons, rows, columns, and background CSS
Drag and drop buttons between slots in edit mode
Create custom Obsidian commands from JavaScript snippets
Save, load, and restore toolbar configurations and minimize to a floating button
disambiguation: Not a theming or appearance plugin; it is a floating command toolbar for the mobile editor.
extras: Custom commands run user-authored JavaScript via the Function constructor; the README warns users not to paste untrusted snippets. The README also includes a section on privacy (no telemetry) and off-topic freelance advertising by the author.
intentEvidence: intentionally replacing parts of the default mobile toolbar/navigation UX
motivation: The author built it around their own mobile workflow and aesthetic tastes and shared it with others who enjoy that style.
problem: Obsidian's default mobile toolbar and navigation are fixed, so users cannot rearrange buttons, add gestures, or control their appearance.

relations.evidence: explore what other plugins add the behavior you want so you can add it to your Gay toolbar

summary: Customizable floating command toolbar for mobile that assigns tap, long-press, and swipe actions to colorful draggable buttons.
